speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help identify the cause of your rash and recent illness, can you describe what the rash looks like and when it first appeared?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: The timeline of facial rash appearing after a week of viral prodrome, sparing the mouth, is highly characteristic of Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease). Does the rash on her trunk have a lacy or net-like appearance, and have her cheeks looked bright red, like she was slapped?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin.

speaker: Doctor
text: The classic "slapped cheek" facial rash followed by a lacy body rash is diagnostic for Erythema Infectiosum, also known as Fifth Disease. No further tests are needed as the clinical presentation is pathognomonic. DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease)
